mechanism_narrative: Transit-station footfall is the leading proxy for discretionary trip-making: the t-0 recovery from -62.0 to -55.0 is the first transit improvement in four observed weeks, and retail footfall follows transit with a two-to-four week lag, lifting the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean above the trailing mean of -58.1.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 11.8 points week-on-week at t-0 while TRANSIT improved 7.0 points
failure_condition: Forward 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is at or below the trailing mean of -58.1 even though the t-0 TRANSIT mean (-55.0) exceeds the t-1w mean (-62.0).

mechanism_narrative: The step-2 policy shock restoring non-essential retail and outdoor hospitality is binding capacity: once TRANSIT crosses above -60 and WORKPLACES recovers above -50, physical shopping capacity is legally and practically restored, so the RETAIL_REC mean over the next two weeks exceeds the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -60 (observed -55.0 at t-0 versus -62.0 at t-1w)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES jumped 8.9 points to -47.4 at t-0, crossing -50
regime_hint: policy reopening step with non-essential retail permitted
failure_condition: In the two weeks after TRANSIT first crosses above -60, RETAIL_REC weekly means stay at or below -58.1.

mechanism_narrative: Discretionary time is split between outdoor parks and indoor destinations; PARKS fell 13.7 points at t-1w and a further 10.0 points at t-0 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 18.9 to 15.6, meaning trips are leaving the home neighbourhood for non-park destinations, and that released flow rotates into retail within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines at least 10 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL declines at least 2 points in the same week
regime_hint: reopening with outdoor-only socialising rules being relaxed
failure_condition: Weeks where PARKS falls at least 10 points and RESIDENTIAL falls at least 2 points are followed by a forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean no higher than the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: Short-run swings are weather-driven rather than policy-driven: the 13.7-point PARKS collapse from 46.0 to 32.3 and its further slide to 22.3 is a spring weather reversion that pushes leisure trips back indoors, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next single week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS path 23.1, 46.0, 32.3, 22.3 across the four weekly means
regime_hint: spring weather regime with volatile park attendance
failure_condition: The week following a greater-than-10-point PARKS decline shows RETAIL_REC no higher than the -50.3 recorded at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: Residential stickiness brakes the retail recovery: RESIDENTIAL has stayed at or above +15.6 in all four observed weeks, and residual home-stay removes commuter and lunchtime retail trips, so if RESIDENTIAL holds above +17 the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean fails to clear the trailing mean of -58.1.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays above +17 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL weekly means 17.1, 16.1, 18.9, 15.6 while WORKPLACES stayed below -44
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above +17 for two consecutive weeks while the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds -58.1, the braking claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Office return and transit use are complements for retail: the joint t-0 improvement of WORKPLACES (-56.3 to -47.4) and TRANSIT (-62.0 to -55.0) rebuilds weekday commuter footfall, and that commuter base is the channel through which retail recovers over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by at least 5 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES +8.9 points and TRANSIT +7.0 points in the same t-0 week
failure_condition: Weeks with joint WORKPLACES and TRANSIT gains of at least 5 points are followed by RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days no higher than the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under an escalating-restriction regime, precautionary behaviour appears first as GROCERY_PHARM suppression and RESIDENTIAL elevation, and discretionary retail is the first category cut, so the forward RETAIL_REC mean falls below the trailing mean when those two series cross their thresholds.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls back below -12 while RESIDENTIAL rises above +18
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged -6.3 to -14.1 and RESIDENTIAL 15.6 to 18.9 over the four weeks
regime_hint: escalating restriction regime driven by variant risk
failure_condition: Under GROCERY_PHARM below -12 and RESIDENTIAL above +18, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is the least-suppressed series at -8.6 versus -50.3 for retail, a roughly 42-point gap that measures pent-up non-essential demand: because essential errands already run near normal, that gap closes upward, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:gap between GROCERY_PHARM (-8.6) and RETAIL_REC (-50.3) at t-0 is 41.7 points
failure_condition: The GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC gap widens or stays constant over the following two weeks while the forward RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the trailing mean.
